FAQ

## Frequently asked questions
Everything you need to know for complete peace of mind.

Can I import testimonials I've already collected?

Yes! Senja allows you to import your existing screen grabs, [video testimonials](/) and text testimonials from 35 sources, including X, Facebook, Google, Capterra, Airbnb, Zillow and TrustPilot. If you'd rather not lift a finger, our [free concierge migration](https://senja.io/p/senja/r/m7VzsW) moves everything over for you.

What information can I collect from my customers?

Our flexible forms allow you to collect anything you want to make up your customer testimonials.

What happens after I collect 15 testimonials?

Once you hit the 15 testimonial limit, new testimonials in your account will be hidden. Your forms and widgets will still work, but to view your new testimonial you will need to upgrade.

What happens if I cancel or downgrade?

You drop to the Free plan at the end of your billing period, with a 10-day grace period on paid features. Your testimonials stay, your forms and widgets keep working, and your links and embeds don't break. Widgets and Walls of Love show Senja branding again, and new testimonials over the 15 free limit are hidden until you upgrade. Download your HD videos before you downgrade, since the Free plan exports in SD.

Can I download my videos and use them anywhere?

Yes. Your testimonials are yours, and every plan includes exports. Video downloads are SD on Free and HD on Starter and Pro. Use them on your website, in ads, wherever you like.

Do you offer discounts to nonprofits / charities?

Yes. You can learn more about our non-profit discount [here](https://support.senja.io/articles/do-you-offer-a-discount-for-non-profits-charities-ng4my).

Do you offer any other discounts?

Yearly billing gets you 2 months free, and registered nonprofits get a discount (see above). We run the occasional seasonal deal too. There's no student discount, and codes from coupon sites aren't ours and won't work.

Which payment formats and currencies do you accept?

All payments on our standard plans are via debit cards and credit card.

We use Stripe, the leading payment processor for SaaS companies.

What happens when I switch from monthly to annual billing?

Stripe prorates the switch: the unused time on your monthly plan is credited toward the annual charge, and your invoice shows the exact amounts. If anything looks off, message support and we'll sort it out.

Can I get invoices with my company details?

Yes. On any paid plan you can view and download invoices from your Billing page and add your company name and billing address. If an older invoice is missing, send support your payment dates and we'll find it.

Do you offer refunds?

We handle refunds case-by-case. Billing errors, unused accounts and missed renewal notices are all fair game. Message support with your account email and your reason, and we'll reply within 1-2 business days. Approved refunds reach your original payment method in 5-10 business days, and your testimonials stay intact either way.

Do you have an agency plan?

Yes! Senja works well for agencies who want to invite multiple clients. [Read this guide](https://support.senja.io/articles/do-you-have-an-agency-plan-qd7ke).

Can I get more projects, seats or forms without changing plans?

Pro includes 5 projects and 5 seats, and you can add more anytime for $10/month per extra project and $5/month per extra seat. Forms come with your plan: 3 on Starter, unlimited on Pro.

Can I transfer a project to a client or another account?

Yes. Message support with the project name and both account emails and we'll move it over. Testimonials, forms and settings all carry across, and your links and embeds keep working. The new owner takes over billing from there.

# 8 free customer case study templates
Eight fill-in-the-blank structures for case studies your customers star in. Copy one into Google Docs, Word or Notion, and publish. Or skip the writing and generate a case study from testimonials you've already collected.

[Generate a case study](https://app.senja.io/signup)

![The Senja dashboard listing collected testimonials, with a generated case study card alongside](/_astro/hero.DTno58O4_1igHwg.webp)

The templates

## Pick a structure and fill in the blanks
Every template follows the same rule: result first, story second, proof throughout. Copy the one that fits and swap in your customer.

### 1. The classic problem-solution-results template
Best for: Your first case study. Works in any industry.

### [Customer name] + [headline result]
Write the result first: “How Marigold Studio cut editing time by 70%”

### Snapshot
Three lines your reader can scan: who the customer is, what they do, and the one number that matters.

- Company: [name, industry, size]
- Challenge: [the problem in one sentence]
- Result: [the headline number]

### The problem
What was broken, and what was it costing them? Use their words. Two or three paragraphs, no more.

### The solution
How they found you, what they tried first, and what your product changed day-to-day. Specific beats impressive: “she sends the form after every project” is better than “streamlined workflows”.

### The results
Two or three numbers with context. Before and after. If you don’t have numbers, use time: “what took a week now takes an afternoon.”

### Pull quote
The single best sentence your customer said. Put it in big type.

### CTA
One line, one link: what should the reader do next?

Copy this template[Generate it from a testimonial](/case-study-generator)

### 2. The one-page case study
Best for: Sales teams who need a leave-behind, and buyers who won’t read 1,000 words.

### [Headline: customer + result]
**Who** — one sentence on the customer.

**Problem** — two sentences, max.

**Fix** — two sentences on what your product did.

**Numbers** — three stats in big type. This is the section people actually read.

**Quote** — one strong customer quote with name, title and photo.

**CTA** — one link.

The rule: if it doesn’t fit on one page, cut the problem section before you cut the numbers.

Copy this template[Generate it from a testimonial](/case-study-generator)

### 3. The testimonial-based case study
Best for: Turning one glowing testimonial into a full story.

Start with the testimonial you already have. Your customer has done the hard part: they’ve told you the result in their own words. Your job is to fill in the story around it.

### Headline
Pull the strongest claim from the testimonial and make it specific: “Senja doubled my conversion rate” becomes “How Marie doubled her course sales page conversion rate”.

### The quote, up top
Open with the full testimonial. It’s your hook and your proof in one.

### The backstory
Ask the customer three follow-up questions: What was going on before? What almost stopped you buying? What surprised you after?

### The detail
Expand each answer into a short section. Keep their phrasing; polish, don’t rewrite.

### The numbers
Pin down any claim in the testimonial. “Way more sales” becomes “38% more sales in the first month”.

### CTA
One line, one link.

Copy this template[Generate it from a testimonial](/case-study-generator)

### 4. The metrics-driven case study
Best for: When you have hard numbers and a data-minded buyer.

### Headline
The biggest number, plainly stated.

### The scoreboard
Open with a before/after list:

- [Metric 1]: before → after
- [Metric 2]: before → after
- [Metric 3]: before → after

### How we measured
One short paragraph on where the numbers come from. This is what makes a skeptical reader trust the rest.

### What drove each number
One section per metric: what changed in their workflow to move it.

### The customer’s read
A quote where the customer interprets the numbers, not just praises you.

### CTA
One line, one link.

Copy this template[Generate it from a testimonial](/case-study-generator)

### 5. The agency client case study
Best for: Agencies and freelancers pitching the next client.

### The brief
What the client hired you to do, in their words.

### The constraint
Budget, timeline, a stubborn stakeholder. Every project has one, and naming it is what makes the win believable.

### The work
Your process in three to five steps. Show one artefact per step if you can: a wireframe, a draft, a before screenshot.

### The outcome
Results tied back to the brief. Did you do the thing they hired you for? Prove it.

### What the client said
Quote, name, company. Video if you have it.

### Work with us
Your CTA, plus one line on what kind of projects you take.

Copy this template[Generate it from a testimonial](/case-study-generator)

### 6. The B2B SaaS case study
Best for: Software with a real sales cycle, where the reader is building a business case.

### Company profile
Industry, team size, tools they already use. Your buyer is checking “are they like us?”

### The trigger
What event made them go looking for a tool? A hire, a failed launch, a spreadsheet that finally broke?

### The evaluation
What else they considered and why they picked you. Don’t skip this; it’s the part prospects screenshot.

### Rollout
How long it took to get value. Be honest; a real timeline is more convincing than “instant”.

### The outcome
Numbers a CFO would accept, plus the day-to-day wins the team actually feels.

### Quote from the decision-maker
And one from a daily user if you can get it.

### CTA
One line, one link.

Copy this template[Generate it from a testimonial](/case-study-generator)

### 7. The interview case study
Best for: Publishing fast, straight from one customer call.

Record a 20-minute call, transcribe it, and edit down. The format is the transcript, lightly cleaned up.

### Intro
Two lines on who you talked to and the result they got.

### The questions (pick six to eight)
- What was going on when you started looking for [product category]?
- What almost stopped you from buying?
- What did the first week look like?
- What’s different now, day-to-day?
- What number would you point to?
- Who would you recommend this to — and who is it not for?
- What would you tell someone on the fence?

### Edit rule
Cut your questions down to one line each, keep their answers nearly verbatim, and bold the sentences you’d want quoted.

### CTA
One line, one link.

Copy this template[Generate it from a testimonial](/case-study-generator)

### 8. The video case study script
Best for: Turning one Zoom call into a video your sales team will actually use.

Total: 90 seconds to 3 minutes. Structure the call so editing is easy.

### Cold open (5–10s)
The customer says the result. No intro, no logo. “We cut onboarding from two weeks to two days.”

### Who they are (15s)
Name, role, company, what the company does.

### The before (30s)
The problem and what it was costing them. Prompt: “Take me back to before you found us.”

### The after (30–45s)
What changed. Prompt: “Walk me through how you use it now.”

### The number (10s)
One stat, said to camera.

### The recommendation (10s)
“If you’re [audience], do [action].”

### Shoot list
The interview, plus 30 seconds of screen recording of them actually using your product. That’s all the b-roll you need.

▶

Copy this template[Generate it from a testimonial](/case-study-generator)

The anatomy

## What every good case study includes
Whichever template you pick, the bones are the same.

1. **A result in the headline** — “How X achieved Y” beats “X case study” every time
2. **A customer snapshot** — who they are, so readers can see themselves
3. **The problem, in their words** — pain they’d recognise, not marketing copy
4. **The turning point** — why they chose you over doing nothing
5. **Specific results** — numbers, timeframes, before-and-after
6. **A pull quote** — the best sentence, in big type
7. **A face and a name** — photo, name, title. Anonymous case studies convince nobody
8. **One CTA** — a single next step, not five

Decisions, decisions

## Which template should you use?
- First case study ever → the classic problem-solution-results
- Buyer with no time → the one-pager
- You already have great testimonials → testimonial-based (or let Senja generate it)
- You have strong data → metrics-driven
- You’re an agency or freelancer → the client template
- Long sales cycle → B2B SaaS
- You need it published this week → the interview
- A willing customer and a camera → the video script

The shortcut

## Or skip the template entirely
Senja turns testimonials you've already collected into finished case studies — summary, metrics, pull quote and all. Pick a testimonial, click generate, edit, share. The template's built in.

- Free to use
- Built from your real testimonials
- Edit everything before you share

[Try the case study generator](/case-study-generator)

![A case study generated by Senja from a testimonial, with summary, metrics and pull quote](/_astro/cs-feature.NDq2Oloy_1zErOT.webp)

Questions

## Case study template FAQs
What should a case study template include?+

Eight things: a results-focused headline, a customer snapshot, the problem, the turning point, specific results, a pull quote, the customer's name and photo, and one CTA. If your template is missing the numbers or the name, fix that first.

How long should a case study be?+

500–1,000 words for a written case study, one page for a sales leave-behind, 90 seconds to 3 minutes for video. Shorter than you think: the reader wants the result and the proof, not the epic.

What format should a case study be in?+

Wherever your buyer already reads: a page on your website for SEO, a PDF one-pager for sales calls, video for social. Start with the web page. It keeps working while you sleep.

What's the difference between a case study and a testimonial?+

A testimonial is the customer's claim ("Senja doubled my sales"). A case study is the story that proves it: the before, the after and the numbers in between. The best case studies are built from testimonials — that's exactly what Senja's case study generator does.

How do I get customers to agree to a case study?+

Ask right after a win, keep the ask small (one 20-minute call), and show them a draft before you publish. Customers who've already left you a glowing testimonial are your warmest list. Start there.

Interviewing a customer first? Steal these [45 case study questions](/blog/case-study-questions).

It’s sitting in a testimonial you collected last month. Give Senja a minute to turn it into a story you can share.
